findings.title: New players cannot start any of the five daily missions — the ₹6,000 change comments out mxPlanDay(1), leaving MX.plan empty
findings.observed: A new game saves MX.plan=[]; no Day 1 mission markers or briefings are created.

findings.title: New Fresher and Topper players start with the wrong energy and vital bars — the new wallet comment disables S.en=enCap()
findings.observed: Fresher starts at 100/140 energy and Topper starts at 100/75.

findings.title: A mission failure at day rollover leaves players moving behind its open failure card — newDay checks the full-screen veil, not the sheet opened by mxFail
findings.observed: mxFail sets UI.sheet=true and S.running=false; newDay(true) immediately sets S.running=true.

findings.title: Players in The Terrace are thrown outside at 23:00 instead of continuing in place — partyUpdate still calls partyExit before the new rollover
findings.observed: At 23:00 partyExit changes the scene to campus and restores the entrance position.

findings.title: Players in the Basement remain on the old day after 23:00 — clUpdate advances the clock but never invokes the rollover
findings.observed: In the cellar the clock passes 23:00 without incrementing the day until the player exits.

findings.title: The four students can repeat their line in the same mission or chai side quest — the roaming rearm flag bypasses the per-mission spoken flag
findings.observed: After leaving for the cooldown and returning, pvArmed replays a line already heard in this run.

findings.title: Players who already heard a student roaming cannot hear them again as the Lost Teammate — mission voice eligibility only checks roles and chai targets
findings.observed: ACT.cur.n holds the lost student, but pvMxDue checks only ACT.cur.targets.

findings.title: Players still hear a newly recorded student's voice after running away from them — slap reactions play the full clip without a distance check or fade
findings.observed: A slap starts a full-volume buffer source that keeps playing after the student leaves range.

findings.title: New players cannot find or sell the first day's collectible loot — the starting-cash edit comments out spawnLoot(1)
findings.observed: ECO.loot stays empty all Day 1 because spawnLoot(1) is inside the // comment.

findings.title: Drivers continuing after a day rollover reload on foot without their car or radio — the new rollover save omits the driven vehicle and radio state
findings.observed: The rollover save has position but no vehicle reference; Continue initializes S.veh to -1.

findings.title: Players lose food and drink purchases and see the wrong wallet after reloading — interactions save before charging and never persist the resulting balance
findings.observed: Buying ₹20 chai saves before the debit, so a reload restores the earlier wallet.

findings.title: Players cannot hear a student again when they promptly leave and return — proximity rearming also requires a 20-second-plus cooldown
findings.observed: A return before 20 seconds plus clip duration cannot rearm the student voice.

findings.title: Players hear overlapping student recordings after slapping a nearby student — hit playback only stops a proximity clip if it belongs to the same student
findings.observed: Slapping another student starts PV.hit while the current PV.cur recording keeps playing.

findings.title: Players miss distinct payouts and repeated important warnings for 45 seconds — toast deduplication strips amounts and applies the minor-message window to important messages
findings.observed: A second +₹150 or +₹200 toast within 45 seconds shares the same normalized key and is dropped.

findings.title: Players lose queued mission or money notifications during a burst — the two-entry toast queue silently discards its oldest important message
findings.observed: A fourth important message shifts the oldest queued important message out without displaying it.

findings.title: Standalone Eye-view drivers see no wet-road streaks from their own vehicle — the newly added reflection list excludes S.veh
findings.observed: The new standalone renderer skips the driven vehicle when building the wet-streak list.

findings.title: Standalone phone drivers cannot read the song artist or full title — the new dashboard hides the artist and truncates titles on touch screens
findings.observed: The standalone touch dashboard hides dashBy and truncates long titles.

findings.title: Standalone drivers repeatedly return to a broken radio after three failed tracks — the new retry loop keeps RADIO.want set
findings.observed: Three standalone radio failures stop playback for 8 seconds, then retries restart.

findings.title: Standalone screen-reader drivers cannot find speed, song or Next — the new dashboard stays aria-hidden when displayed
findings.observed: The standalone visible dashboard and Next button remain inside aria-hidden="true".

findings.title: Drivers still see the previous Radio on message over silence after skipping — the revised radioSkip removes state without rerendering the toast
findings.observed: Skipping removes the toast from the array but leaves its old DOM visible during a stall.

findings.title: Phone drivers can lose the dashboard after rotating from portrait to landscape — the portrait-only inline top overrides the landscape CSS
findings.observed: The portrait-computed inline top remains on the dashboard after rotating to landscape.

findings.title: Players see the previous day's prize counted again in the next day's earnings — rollover resets daily stats without updating ECO.lastRs after settlement
findings.observed: A ₹1,500 prize and ₹400 rent add ₹1,100 to the next day's earned total.

findings.title: Phone players cannot read their completed-day earnings, prize and wallet summary — rollover puts the entire summary in a single ellipsized toast
findings.observed: The day summary is one nowrap line truncated with an ellipsis on narrow screens.

findings.title: Standalone Eye-view Lost Teammate players get no target column — the new renderer reads a waypoint the lost quest never supplies
findings.observed: The new standalone Eye renderer uses UI.sideWp, which remains null for Lost Teammate.

findings.title: Standalone Eye-view Impostor players cannot see the final meeting destination — the new marker pass uses points() without Main Hall
findings.observed: The new standalone Eye renderer marks Impostor teammates but not the final meeting hall.

findings.title: Standalone Eye-view players can miss a daytime waypoint — the new cyan column has little contrast against the pale sky
findings.observed: The standalone daytime cyan waypoint is a 35%-opacity column against the pale sky.

findings.title: Standalone players on slow devices wait much longer for stalled radio tracks to skip — the new watchdog sums frame time capped at 50 ms
findings.observed: At 5 rendered frames/s the standalone 7-second watchdog takes about 28 real seconds.

findings.title: Players can hear one of the four recordings without approaching its student — a remote chain collision starts the student's hit voice without a proximity check
findings.observed: A distant chain-reaction collision calls pvHit without checking player-to-student distance.

findings.title: Players lose an in-progress mission or side quest and its spoken-line state on reload — the save omits active runs and Continue clears the current mission
findings.observed: Continue restores MX.plan but explicitly sets MX.cur=null and never restores ACT.cur.

findings.title: Players on slow phones get days four times longer than the intended new pace — the slowed clock sums frame deltas capped at 50 ms
findings.observed: At 5 FPS the 08:00–23:00 day takes about 40 minutes, not about 10 minutes.

findings.title: Players can lose queued mission or money messages after skipping a song — radioSkip empties the visible toast without advancing the queue
findings.observed: Removing the active radio toast leaves toastQ nonempty but no active toast to expire it.

findings.title: Standalone players still get stacked notifications at every rollover — the documented game retains the old three-toast renderer instead of the new queue
findings.observed: A standalone rollover pushes both the day summary and new-day toast simultaneously.

findings.title: Players see road-food purchases and traffic fines doubled in the day summary — both the transaction and ecoStep add each debit to spent
findings.observed: A ₹40 bakery purchase adds ₹80 to the day's spent total although the wallet loses ₹40.

findings.title: Players continuing an all-nighter checkpoint return to 22:59 instead of the saved early-morning time — applySave clamps every saved clock to before 23:00
findings.observed: Continuing a 02:00 all-nighter checkpoint clamps S.t to 22:59 of the previous evening.

findings.title: Players miss a minor hint on retry even though it never appeared — the toast records a message as seen before deciding to drop it
findings.observed: A minor toast dropped behind another is still marked seen and cannot appear for 45 seconds.

findings.title: Eye-view players cannot identify which student is speaking — the speaker name is rendered only in the obscured 2D view
findings.observed: The speaker's name is drawn only on the hidden 2D canvas, not in the Eye view scene or HUD.

findings.title: Standalone Eye-view drivers cannot take a clean photo — the newly added dashboard is not hidden in photo mode
findings.observed: Entering Photo mode leaves the standalone driving dashboard over the photo frame.

findings.title: Players are told the new day has zero objectives when it actually has five missions — the rollover announcement counts the emptied legacy MISSIONS array
findings.observed: The new-day toast says 0 objectives although MX.plan contains 5 missions.

findings.title: Muted students speak unexpectedly when players later unmute beside them — zero dialogue volume freezes proximity and mission spoken flags
findings.observed: With Dialogue at 0, the proximity loop returns before updating spoken or rearm flags.

findings.title: Players hear two student voices briefly when the nearest speaker changes — the old clip fades for 0.2 seconds while the next clip starts
findings.observed: Switching speakers stops the first source after 0.22 s but starts the next after 0.01 s.

findings.title: Players beside two students can keep hearing the farther student's line — speaker switching requires the new nearest student to be 40 units closer
findings.observed: When A is 90 units away and B is 80, A continues speaking because 80 is not below 50.
